newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Danzas looks to restructuring gains.
newsitem.headline: Danzas looks to restructuring gains.

text.p: Swiss-based freight forwarding group Danzas AG said it is near completion of a major restructuring which should significantly boost results.
"There is still much to be done," said chief executive officer Peter Wagner in a news briefing to detail the group's 1996 results. "A new Danzas is emerging," he added.
"The group's restructuring project, which is expected to boost operating income substantially starting in 1998, progressed on schedule," Danzas said in its annual report.
The company is looking ahead after group operating income was "a disappointing 8.0 million Swiss francs ($5.4 million)" in 1996, outgoing chairman Peter Gross said.
Gross will step down after the annual shareholders' meeting June 6. The company said already last year it planned to name Hanspeter Braendli, on the board since 1996, as new chairman.
Net profit for 1996 was 13 million francs, up from six million in 1995. Net sales totalled 4.05 billion versus 4.02 billion in 1995. Sales were slightly lower in local currencies.

Results in the 1997 first quarter improved slightly compared with the first quarter of 1996, and continued to gain in April. The outcome for the year would depend on the economy, especially in Europe.
Wagner declined to give a detailed prognosis for the year, but noted that the concern has costs "under control".

The group is in phase four of a restructuring begun in 1995, which has included cutting costs and jobs, and in future will focus on optimising its three main divisions: Eurocargo, logistics and intercontinental activities.
It is investing more in data processing and telecommunications while it reduces costs in some other areas.

The "Eurofit" phase of its restructuring, begun last year, was a major factor reducing its workforce by 6.9 percent, to 15,715. Perhaps as many as 1,000 more jobs will be terminated in the current year. Danzas' management said it would first discuss any such plans for further cuts within the company.
It also said it is in the process of closing over 40 cargo terminals, the majority of which are rented rather than owned.
Meanwhile its European cooperation with United Parcel Service UPS signed last year will be expanded, and the companies plan to use joint sales potential.
Danzas has expanded its global office network, but said its main focus on the international side would be to upgrade sales offices in Latin America and Asia to operating companies.

Danzas management said U.K. investor Nicholas Berry, who mounted a campaign last year to wrest more shareholder value from the firm, remained a major shareholder, but with less than five percent. Danzas shareholders rejected Berry's bid to take a seat on the board at last year's annual general meeting.
The company said relations with Berry were normal.
"We could describe them (relations) as the same as with every large shareholder, whereby we make painfully sure that we give him no advantageous information," Gross said.
